title: InfraTrust report: 33 of 38 advisories with known-exploited flaws fixed bundled software components
date_note: The page gives only its own publication day, 25 November.
summary: BleepingComputer reports on an InfraTrust report that tracks 373 new security advisories published by 23 infrastructure vendors, covering 3,880 vulnerabilities. According to the report, 38 contained vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, and 33 of those 38 advisories fixed exploited flaws in bundled software components, primarily PHP, Node.js, and OpenSSH.
plain: A report on infrastructure vendors' security advisories says 38 included flaws on CISA's known-exploited list, and 33 of those 38 fixed flaws in bundled components such as PHP, Node.js and OpenSSH.
exec: The InfraTrust report says exposure to exploited flaws depends on how quickly each vendor rebuilds its products after an upstream fix ships.
action: The InfraTrust report advises removing management interfaces from the Internet and segmenting them internally to limit lateral movement.
